prs.title: fix(optimize-locales-plugin): type Turbopack loader locales as a mutable array
prs.author: costajohnt
prs.body:
Closes #10880

`optimizeLocales.turbopack()` declares each loader's options as `{locales: readonly string[]}`. Next's `TurbopackLoaderOptions` is `Record<string, JSONValue>`, and `JSONValue[]` is a mutable array, so spreading the returned `rules` into a typed `NextConfig` fails with TS2322 even though the rule works at runtime. This changes the declared loader option to `string[]`, which is the change suggested in the issue. The `Options` input type stays `readonly string[]`, so callers can still pass `as const` arrays. Only the shape handed to Next changes.

I checked it against `next@16.4.2` and TypeScript 6.0.3 (`strict`) with a `next.config.ts` covering a single config, a conditioned list, a readonly `as const` locales array, and a `path`/`content` RegExp condition. With the current declaration all four report TS2322 (`The type 'readonly string[]' is 'readonly' and cannot be assigned to the mutable type 'JSONValue[]'`). With this change `tsc --noEmit` passes.

prs.title: feat: add focus events to Table rows
prs.author: dagemawinegash
prs.body:
Adds `onFocus`, `onBlur`, and `onFocusChange` to Table `Row`, allowing applications to update previews or other UI when a row gains or loses focus.

Uses the existing `useFocus` hook, matching `GridListItem`. Callbacks report focus on the row itself; focus inside a cell or button remains separate. Includes regression tests and a Storybook example.

Part of https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/6460 (Table Row only).

prs.title: fix: measure TabPanels after nested content renders and stop size variable inheritance
prs.author: jsabutis
prs.body:
Closes #10292

TabPanels measures its new size in the same commit that mounts the new panel. A nested Tabs has not rendered its TabList and TabPanel yet at that point, so the outer panel animates to the wrong height and snaps when it resets to auto. Also, `--tab-panel-height` and `--tab-panel-width` are only set on the outer TabPanels during the animation, so a nested TabPanels inherits the outer pixel value.

The fix measures and starts the transition in a `requestAnimationFrame` scheduled from the layout effect (still before paint, after the nested collection has flushed), and makes every TabPanels define both variables inline as `auto`. #10293 only changed the inheritance, which is why it had no visible effect.

prs.title: feat: support description text in tree items
prs.author: minwookshin
prs.body:
Closes #10665

Tree items need a description slot that follows the existing GridList accessibility behavior. `Text slot="description"` now uses the inherited `aria-labelledby` relationship, so the row name includes its description. This removes the Tree-specific override and adds the slot, story, documentation, and static naming regressions. The shared GridList hook is unchanged.

Implemented with OpenAI Codex.

prs.title: fix keyboard interaction when combobox and popover have different shadow roots
prs.author: chirokas
prs.body:
Closes

When ComboBoxInput and Popover are rendered in separate shadow DOM trees,
opening the popover via keyboard fails because the relatedTarget of the
virtualBlur event gets retargeted to the nearest shadow-including ancestor,
causing the popover to close unexpectedly.

This fix ensures keyboard interaction works correctly even when the components
don't share the same shadow root.

prs.title: fix(ComboBox): don't commit value on blur when isReadOnly
prs.author: mangeshraut712
prs.body:
## Summary
A read-only ComboBox still ran `commitValue()` on blur. When both `value` and `inputValue` are controlled and the selected item is not in the collection (e.g. async items not loaded yet), that path fires change events and apps that derive input text from the selection can clear a field the user never changed.

Skip the blur commit when `isReadOnly` is set.

Closes #10846

## Test plan
- [x] RAC ComboBox: controlled `isReadOnly` with a value missing from the collection does not fire `onChange` / `onSelectionChange` on blur
